Subject: Dedicated capacity plan for renewal

Hi Aditya,

Quick note as we start our renewal planning — our usage profile for Q3/Q4 has become more bursty than we expected. We saw several short spikes where p50 latency remained fine but p95/p99 token-per-second cost jumped and throttles hit our endpoints.

We're approaching our renewal window (dec 15) and want to discuss options: add a tranche of reserved GPUs, a staged top-up model, or keep current commit and rely more on burst capacity. We attached the weekly usage export for the last 12 weeks.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood propose a sizing approach that avoids over-committing while preventing repeated throttling?
- Is there a way to gate top-ups by utilization (e.g., automatically add headroom if sustained >80% util for 7 days)?
- Rough ARR impact for a conservative top-up vs an aggressive one (ballpark is fine now).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Sofia Gomez
Head of Platform
SparkByte

High level we can do two complementary levers:

2) Utilization gating (automation) — we can configure automated top-ups or burst reallocation when sustained utilization crosses thresholds.

Marissa / Mina — can you review the usage file and propose a short plan (commercial bands + technical gating thresholds). I can then propose a package to SparkByte and share a signed addendum template.

Quick analysis from the CSV and our capacity model:
- Typical baseline utilization: 42% across Q3.
- Short spikes to 88-93% for 2-6 hour windows, about 6 occurrences in 12 weeks.
- Sustained multi-day ramp events (48+ hours) were rare (1 event).

Commercial proposal (ballpark):
A) Conservative: +10 GPUs reserved immediately, include 20% burst credits. Estimated ARR impact: ~ $280k/yr.
B) Staged proportional top-up (recommended): +5 GPUs now, with contractual conditional top-ups of +5 GPUs at 80% sustained util for 7 days, and another +10 GPUs if 85% sustained for 14 days. Cap at +20 GPUs. Estimated ARR in year 1 (if all tranches triggered): ~ $640k.
C) Aggressive: +20 GPUs now. ARR: ~ $560k/yr (higher upfront).

Operational terms to propose to SparkByte:
- Utilization gating automation handled by Redwood control plane (we will only bill for reserved tranche once triggered and accepted via DocuSign or via pre-approved gating).
- 30-day cooldown between tranche triggers to avoid oscillation.
- Monthly utilization reporting and a one-click rollback option if they want to reverse a tranche within 14 days (pro-rated credit).

I attached a quick spreadsheet with the band math and an addendum template.

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity plan for renewal — technical notes

Adding technical context and a recommended runbook for gating + top-up automation:

Summary recommendations:
1) Immediate +5 GPUs (mixed A100/80GB equivalent) to handle median headroom.
2) Configure utilization monitor: p95 slot utilization across model routes + KV cache hit rate. Trigger rule: sustained >80% p95 slot utilization for 7 consecutive rolling days. Secondary trigger: spike rule if >=4 events in 30 days with duration >3 hours.
3) On trigger: provision tranche as standby reserved capacity in the customer27s Dedicated pool in their region, but hold billing until (a) customer accepts the addendum via DocuSign OR (b) pre-approved auto-accept flag is set (customer choice).
4) Autoscale safety: implement a soft-fallback policy that routes excess requests to a compatible quantized variant at slightly higher latency but lower cost if immediate capacity not available.
5) Observability: expose per-route token latency, slot queue length, and tranche-status webhooks for SparkByte to integrate with their SRE alerts.

Sizing calc (very short):
- Current committed GPUs: 40
- Current mean GPU utilization: 42% -> ~16 effective GPUs used
- Spikes require additional 8-12 GPUs to maintain p95 targets. Hence +5 immediate + conditional +5 + +10 final cap.

I'll attach the technical runbook and a sample API payload for the gating webhook.

Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

What we propose now:
- Immediate: +5 GPUs reserved (effective 2026-11-15), 20% burst credits included, pro-rated for remainder of contract year.
- Auto-gating policy: triggers conditional +5 GPUs if sustained >80% p95 slot utilization for 7 days. Triggering requires one of: (1) customer auto-accept flag, or (2) DocuSign approval (link below) — you choose.
- Cap: +20 GPUs total across the renewal term. 30-day cooldown between triggers.
- Observatory delivery: weekly utilization report and real-time webhook (sample in tech runbook).

Commercials / next steps:
